title: Not converted by freedom alone
source_text: XCI. Similiter juxta hunc Doctorem affirmandum non est, existentibus in duobus adultis aequalibus auxiliis gratiae praevenientis, illum qui convertitur, pro sola sua libertate converti. Quoniam licet conversio illa a libertate pendeat, fiatque ab arbitrio pro sua libertate; non tamen fit pro sola sua libertate, sed cooperante simul auxilio gratiae praevenientis per influxum a quo sortitur rationem gratiae cooperantis: quamvis cum hic praesto sit, gratiamque praevenientem dependenter a cooperatione arbitrii comitetur, solum exigatur cooperatio libera arbitrii nostri. Disputatione quadragesima ad articulum 13. quaestionis 14. paragr. ad secundam.
pass_a_gloss: XCI. Likewise according to this Doctor it is not to be affirmed, equal aids of prevenient grace existing in two adults, that he who is converted, is converted by his liberty alone. Since although that conversion depends on liberty, and comes about from choice by its liberty; yet it does not come about by its liberty alone, but with the aid of prevenient grace cooperating at the same time through an influx from which it obtains the character of cooperating grace: although when this is at hand, and accompanies prevenient grace dependently on the cooperation of choice, only the free cooperation of our choice is required. Disputation forty on article 13. of question 14. paragraph on the second.
pass_b_english: Thesis XCI. In the same way, according to this Doctor, one must not say that when two adults have equal aids of prevenient grace, the one who is converted is converted by his freedom alone. That conversion does depend on freedom and is brought about by choice in its freedom. But it is not brought about by that freedom alone: the aid of prevenient grace cooperates with it at the same time, through the influence by which it takes on the character of cooperating grace.

Even so, when that influence is present and accompanies prevenient grace in dependence on the cooperation of choice, nothing more is required than the free cooperation of our choice. This is in disputation 40 on article 13 of question 14, in the paragraph 'Ad secundam'.

lemmas.gloss: obtains the character of cooperating grace

lemmas.latin: solum exigatur cooperatio libera arbitrii nostri
lemmas.gloss: only the free cooperation of our choice is required

choices.why: The same grace as it flows into the act that free choice elicits; its influence depends on consent.

bible_refs: Luis de Molina SJ, Concordia liberi arbitrii cum gratiae donis (Lisbon, 1588), question 14, article 13, disputation 40.
